newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris bourse rise seen muted in '97 after '96 gain.
newsitem.headline: Paris bourse rise seen muted in '97 after '96 gain.

text.p: After gaining more than 23 percent this year, the French stockmarket is expected to rise further in 1997, although market experts predict a smaller advance.

Analysts, portfolio managers and sales strategists interviewed by Reuters generally do not see the blue chip CAC 40 index rising much above 2,450 points and they expect most of that gain to occur in the first half of 1997.
The index closed at 2,318.63 points on Monday, up 23.86 percent so far this year.

"There's no reason for that to change," he said. He said industry and corporate restructurings -- a source of big stock gains -- are set to continue. He expects a further increase in stock prices of 12 to 15 percent.

Georges De Nesmeskeri-Kiss, strategist at Societe Generale, said there was "room for more mergers and acquisitions" along the lines of Axa-UAP in the financial sector and Auchan-Docks de France in the retail sector.
He expects the CAC to reach 2,450 points in 1997.

Although he expects the bulk of the increase to occur in the first half, the placement of a huge stake of state-owned France Telecom on the bourse in the spring may slow the advance. Analysts estimate the state will put between 20 and 40 billion francs of France Telecom shares on the market.
Michele Jardin, a strategist at Credit Lyonnais Securities, said she expected the market to perform moderately well next year and expects the CAC to reach 2,400 points by summer.
She noted its rise this year has lagged gains in other European bourses, such as Frankfurt, up 26 percent, and Madrid, up 40 percent.

One chartist at a brokerage house said he believed the CAC index was nearing the end of a cycle, which would lift it to between 2,380 and 2,450 points early next year but then lead to a sharp correction to as low as 2,150 points by spring.
Speculation is expected to centre on pharmaceuticals, such as Rhone-Poulenc, financial firms, and retailers.
Some market operators said they hoped the new year would usher more transparency and fair play in the market.

"We need to go further toward protecting minority shareholders," one portfolio manager said. "We can't understand why the (bourse regulator) COB doesn't take action or suspend shares after imprudent statements by their managers."
